niche: connected TV and streaming advertising agency
prompt_text: What is the best connected TV advertising agency?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: There isn’t a single “best” connected TV (CTV) advertising agency — the right partner depends on your goals (brand vs. performance), budget, geography, desired platforms (Roku, Hulu, YouTube/YouTube TV, Samsung, Vizio, MVPDs, etc.), and whether you need creative, media buying, data/measurement or all of the above.

How to pick the best CTV agency for you
- Define your objective: reach/awareness, frequency control, audience-based performance (conversions, site visits), or direct-response.
- Decide buying method: programmatic (DSP-based) vs. direct/premium (publisher deals/guaranteed buys).
- Know your measurement needs: reach and frequency, completed-view rates, brand lift, attribution to conversions, third‑party verification.
- Check platform relationships: preferred access to Roku, Samsung, Hulu/Disney/Peacock, Sling, Vizio, YouTube, etc.
- Ask about identity and privacy approaches: CTV IDs, probabilistic vs deterministic matching, and compliance with current regulations.
- Request case studies with metrics for campaigns like yours and references.

Types of agencies and examples
- Large global media groups (best for scale, publisher relationships, global rollout, integrated measurement): GroupM (Mindshare/Wavemaker/MediaCom), Omnicom Media Group (OMD/PHD), Publicis Media (Starcom/Zenith), Dentsu (Carat/Vizeum), IPG Mediabrands. These have deep CTV teams and programmatic + direct-buy capabilities.
- Specialist/full-stack CTV providers (good when you want platform expertise or integrated ad tech): Amobee, Simulmedia, and major DSPs/platforms used by agencies such as The Trade Desk and Roku OneView (platform solution). Innovid and Innovid-like vendors are strong for CTV creative and measurement.
- Independent/ boutique agencies (best for highly tailored strategy, creative-first or performance-focused needs): local or niche shops with CTV/OTT focus — good if you need hands-on service and creative + media alignment.

Key questions to ask any agency
- Which CTV platforms and publishers do you have direct deals with? Can you guarantee inventory?
- Do you buy programmatically? Which DSPs/SSPs do you use?
- How do you measure viewability, completed views, reach/frequency and conversions? Which third‑party vendors do you use (Nielsen, Comscore, Innovid, Moat/DoubleVerify, SambaTV)?
- What targeting signals do you use (household, device, behavioral, contextual) and how do you handle privacy?
- Can you show campaign case studies relevant to our vertical/goal with metrics?
- What are your creative capabilities for CTV (long/short spots, interactive, dynamic creative)?
- How do you handle reporting cadence and attribution?

If you want a quick starting shortlist
- For global scale and integrated media: pick an agency in a major holding group (Mindshare/OMD/Starcom/Zenith/etc.).
- For programmatic and sophisticated targeting: work with a team that uses The Trade Desk or Amobee and has DSP expertise.
- For premium publisher access and platform-native campaigns: look at agencies/partners that have direct Roku, Hulu, Samsung, Vizio relationships or work with Simulmedia/Roku OneView.

If you tell me your region, budget, campaign objective, and whether you need creative and measurement, I’ll recommend 3–5 agencies/partners that would likely be the best fit and what to ask them.
